To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the critical current diffraction patterns of SIFS Josephson tunnel junction arrays with local variation of critical current density are in good agreement with simulations.

the step height of a Nb/AlOx/NiCu/Nbx stack can be controlled with optical lithography and that the critical current diffraction patterns of SIFS Josephson junctions with local variation of critical current density are in good agreement with simulations.

we have fabricated and characterized Josephson tunnel junction with a thickness step of the metallic interlayer and demonstrated the feasibility of using the stepped Josephson junction for the study of local variation of the critical current density in a superconductor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication, analysis, and modeling of SIFS Josephson junctions with a center thickness step and a local variation of the critical current density.
the fabrication and investigation of Josephson tunnel junction with a step in the center and a local variation of the critical current density.
the influence of local variation of the critical current density in the ferromagnetic interlayer of a SIFS junction on the critical current diffraction patterns.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the critical current density is not affected by the step in the NiCu interlayer.
the junctions with the center step are a good tool for the study of Josephson junctions and the effect of the step in the middle of the Josephson junction on the critical current.
the step in the NiCu layer does not affect the Josephson properties of the SIFS junctions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a local variation of the critical current density can be realized by a step in the metallic interlayer.
a local control of the critical current density can be achieved by a small step in the metallic interlayer of SIFS Josephson junctions.
the fabrication of stepped junctions is feasible and that the critical current diffraction can be used for the characterization of the local critical current density in a Josephson junction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical current density in the SIFS junction is not uniform and the critical current density of the etched part is smaller than the non-etched one.
the critical current diffraction can serve as a tool for measuring local variations in the critical current density.
the step position can be controlled by optical lithography.
